chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ḥassān, from Abī ʿImrān al-Armanī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a sound man who gouged out the eye of a one-eyed man. He said: “The full diyah is upon him. If the one whose eye was gouged wishes to take qisas from his companion and take five thousand dirhams from him, he may do so, because the full diyah belongs to him, and he has taken half of it through qisas.”

key_terms.أَعْوَرَ: a one-eyed person who has only one functioning eye
key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: financial blood-compensation legally due for bodily injury
key_terms.بِالْقِصَاصِ: by means of qisas, the law of retaliation
key_terms.خَمْسَةَ آلَافِ دِرْهَمٍ: five thousand dirhams as monetary compensation
key_terms.صَحِيحٍ: a physically sound person with no such impairment
key_terms.يَقْتَصَّ: to exact qisas, meaning retaliatory legal retribution

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a healthy man gouges out the eye of a one-eyed man in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning injury to the remaining eye of a one-eyed man. It establishes that the full diyah is due, and that the injured party may combine qisas with financial compensation amounting to half the diyah, since the qisas accounts for the other half.
